title: Box Breathing Technique
description: A powerful breathing exercise to calm your nervous system before performances.
howTo: Inhale for 4 counts, hold for 4 counts, exhale for 4 counts, hold for 4 counts. Repeat 5-10 times. This activates your parasympathetic nervous system and reduces anxiety.

title: Progressive Muscle Relaxation
description: Release physical tension that accompanies stage fright.
howTo: Starting from your toes, tense each muscle group for 5 seconds, then release. Work your way up through your legs, core, arms, and face. This helps you recognize and release tension.

title: Positive Visualization
description: Mental rehearsal of a successful performance to build confidence.
howTo: Close your eyes and vividly imagine yourself performing flawlessly. Engage all senses—see the audience, hear the music, feel the stage beneath your feet. Practice this 5-10 minutes before performance.

title: Grounding Technique (5-4-3-2-1)
description: Bring yourself back to the present moment when anxiety strikes.
howTo: Notice 5 things you see, 4 things you can touch, 3 things you hear, 2 things you smell, and 1 thing you taste. This anchors you to reality and away from anxious thoughts.

title: Physical Warm-up & Movement
description: Use movement to transform nervous energy into positive energy.
howTo: Do light cardio, stretching, or dance. This releases endorphins, reduces cortisol, and channels nervous energy into your performance. Even 10 minutes makes a difference.

title: Positive Affirmations
description: Reframe your mindset with powerful, encouraging statements.
howTo: Repeat affirmations like 'I am prepared and ready,' 'My voice is strong,' 'I own this stage,' or 'I bring this character to life.' Say them with conviction and belief.

title: Pre-Show Ritual
description: Create a consistent routine that signals to your brain it's showtime.
howTo: Develop a personal ritual: specific music, meditation, lucky charm, or pep talk. Consistency builds confidence and helps manage anxiety through familiarity.

title: Reframe Nervousness as Excitement
howTo: When you feel butterflies, say 'I'm excited!' instead of 'I'm nervous.' Nervousness and excitement have the same physical symptoms—your mind interprets them based on your narrative.

title: Connect with Your Scene Partners
description: Use social connection to ease anxiety.
howTo: Before the show, spend time with your cast mates. Share encouragement, humor, or a group circle. Connection reduces isolation and reminds you you're not alone.

title: Journaling
description: Process emotions and thoughts before they become overwhelming.
howTo: Write about your fears, hopes, or worries. This externalizes anxiety and helps you see situations more objectively. You can also write about successful past performances.
